solutions.check: grid and clues read from the Guardian's printable copy, its numbering matching the numbers printed in it and the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Scare in Scots financial broadsheet, full-flavoured within

indicators.note: within says one piece sits inside the other, so the newspaper is opened up to take the richness

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times, a British broadsheet newspaper
full-flavoured food is rich

explanation.surface: A Scottish financial paper runs a scare story about something rich and tasty inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scare in Scots' is the definition: the word belongs to Scottish dialect, and 'within' places the richness inside the newspaper's initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Scots dialect word for a fright, a sudden alarm.

clue.text: Part of string section beats time for stuff

parts.note: the violins of an orchestra's strings are fiddles
a clock ticks, beating out the time

explanation.surface: A violinist in the string section taps out the rhythm instead of playing.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are dismissive exclamations meaning nonsense, as in 'stuff and nonsense'.

clue.text: Repeated sport for NZ nightbird

indicators.note: repeated asks for the short sport's letters to be given twice over

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a sport much played in New Zealand

explanation.surface: A New Zealand owl is named after a sport said twice.
explanation.definitionFit: A Maori name for the morepork, a small New Zealand owl that calls at night.

clue.text: Centre of faith wavering, broken by severe Islamic services

indicators.note: broken by says the shuffled letters are split open with another piece set inside
wavering says those central letters are unsteady and rearranged
centre of picks out the inner letters of the word faith, dropping its ends

parts.note: a bad cold is a severe one

explanation.surface: A believer's core faith wavers, shaken by harsh treatment at religious services.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wavering' rearranges the inner letters of 'faith' to IAT, and 'broken by' splits that after its first letter to take the harsh word.
explanation.definitionFit: Arabic-derived term for acts of worship and religious observances in Islam.

clue.text: The old agree about splitting leave

indicators.note: splitting means one piece goes into the middle of the other, dividing it

parts.note: a conge (congé) is leave to depart, a dismissal
RE means about, concerning

explanation.surface: People of the past agreed to split their leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The old' marks the answer as an obsolete word.
explanation.definitionFit: Obsolete verb meaning to be in accord, to harmonise; the label marks its age.

clue.text: Type of vaccine, cube maybe swallowed three times daily

indicators.note: swallowed says the medical abbreviation takes the stock cube inside it

parts.note: TID (ter in die) is the prescription abbreviation for three times daily
Oxo is a British brand of stock cube; maybe marks it as an example

explanation.surface: A vaccine taken like a pill, three times a day, cube perhaps swallowed whole.
explanation.walkthrough: OXO is a familiar British stock-cube brand; TID is prescription shorthand.
explanation.definitionFit: A bacterial toxin made harmless but still able to raise immunity, used in vaccines such as tetanus.

clue.text: School science subject in short, child trailing in clumsy patch

indicators.note: trailing says the child comes after the school subject

parts.note: BOT is short for botany

explanation.surface: A school botany lesson ends with a child trailing about in a messy patch of garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A clumsily made repair or patch is a bungled piece of work.

clue.text: Pass, last dropped, making veteran smoulder?

indicators.note: last dropped tells us to remove the final letter of the Alpine pass

parts.note: the Brenner Pass crosses the Alps between Austria and Italy

explanation.surface: An old soldier's ardour fades on an Alpine pass, the last of his fire dying down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'veteran' marks the answer as an archaic word.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic spelling of burn, so a 'veteran' (old) word for smoulder.

clue.text: Dress material, old, found in hat

indicators.note: found in says the abbreviation for old is placed inside the slang word for hat

parts.note: tile is old slang for a hat

explanation.surface: Old dress fabric turns up in a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A light linen or cotton fabric used for dresses, and the trial garment made from it.

clue.text: The sound of cavalry approaching line in force?

indicators.note: in places the line abbreviation within the police

parts.note: the police force, the cops

explanation.surface: The hoofbeats of approaching horsemen, a line of mounted police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'force?' hints at mounted police, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Hooves striking the road make a clip-clopping noise as horses near.

clue.text: Sea mist shrouding rees fluttering in umbellifer (8, apostrophe)

indicators.note: shrouding says the mist wraps round the other letters

parts.note: haar is a cold sea fog on the east coasts of Scotland and England

indicators.note: fluttering says the letters of rees move about into a new order

explanation.surface: Sea fog drifts over flapping bird life around a wild plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fluttering' rearranges the bird letters as RESE, and 'shrouding' wraps the Scottish sea fog round them, split after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant of the genus Bupleurum, which belongs to the carrot family of umbellifers.

clue.text: King occupying hidden house rented privately (12, three words)

indicators.note: occupying puts the king abbreviation inside the reshuffled letters
hidden suggests the letters are disguised and rearranged out of recognition

parts.note: R is Rex, king

explanation.surface: A monarch secretly lives in a hidden rented property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hidden' is an unusual anagram signal, meaning disguised; 'occupying' sets the king inside the jumble. The rose was an old emblem of secrecy.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin sub rosa: the rose was a symbol of secrecy, so the phrase means confidentially.

clue.text: Navigational aid for sailors once on patrol at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Old sailors on patrol at sea relied on this aid.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval book of sailing directions with harbour charts, a pilot guide for mariners.

clue.text: Local droning noise spread during transmission of data

indicators.note: during places one piece in the course of the other

parts.note: DT is the abbreviation for data transmission
ink that spreads ran

explanation.surface: A humming noise spreads through a data link.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' marks a dialect word.
explanation.definitionFit: Dialect word for a drawl or monotonous drone.

clue.text: Inlet I entered in watery crossing

indicators.note: entered in says the letter goes into the crossing place

parts.note: a ford is a shallow place to cross a river

explanation.surface: I waded across a stream into a coastal inlet.
explanation.definitionFit: A long narrow sea inlet between cliffs, as in Norway.

clue.text: Disused dagger, ineffective with edge half gone, getting oiled?

parts.note: a dud is something that fails to work

indicators.note: half gone tells us to lose the first two of the four letters of edge

parts.note: oiled is slang for drunk, and a bit 'on' means tipsy

explanation.surface: An old dagger, blunt and useless, is being given a coat of oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting oiled?' reads like maintenance but means drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: An obsolete name for a dagger with a hilt of boxwood; 'disused' flags its age.

clue.text: Record? Two couples left kept awake when it's spinning

indicators.note: a spinning record turns round, so the remaining letters are read backwards
left means gone away, so the letter pairs depart from the word

parts.note: someone kept awake is sleepless
two couples are two pairs of letters, here the pair SL and the pair SS

explanation.surface: Two couples left a party that kept them awake while the record went round.
explanation.walkthrough: From SLEEPLESS the pairs SL and SS leave, giving EEPLE, read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A spelt-out form of LP, long-playing record; the question mark flags the wordplay.

clue.text: Scholarship? Inclined to accept first from redbrick

indicators.note: to accept says the slanting word takes the letter inside it

parts.note: leaning means inclined

indicators.note: first from picks out the opening letter of redbrick

explanation.surface: A university scholarship inclined to accept candidates from a redbrick university.
explanation.walkthrough: A redbrick is a British university founded in the Victorian era.
explanation.definitionFit: Scholarship as erudition, knowledge acquired by study.

clue.text: Riding east, stop taking in volunteers

indicators.note: taking in says the stop holds the volunteers inside

parts.note: a quint is an organ stop sounding a fifth above
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: A rider heading east stops to pick up volunteers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stop' is an organ stop, not a halt.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin-derived adjective meaning on horseback, mounted.

clue.text: Beginners fretted, seen losing head, in a pickle

indicators.note: in a pickle means in a mess, so the letters are jumbled
losing head means the first letter of seen is removed

explanation.surface: Novices fretted and were seen in a terrible mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' cuts SEEN to EEN; 'in a pickle' then rearranges FRETTED with EEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of a word for a raw newcomer or novice.

clue.text: Grass ignoring cue to spill the beans, owning up

indicators.note: ignoring says the word cue is left out of the grass

parts.note: fescue is a kind of grass
to sing is slang for to inform or confess

explanation.surface: A grass, ignoring his cue, spills the beans and confesses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' looks like the slang for an informer but is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal participle meaning confessing, admitting the truth.

clue.text: Sickly drink? At first swallowing very little

parts.note: to sup is to drink

indicators.note: swallowing means the first word takes the small one inside it

parts.note: erst is an archaic word for at first, formerly
wee means very little

explanation.surface: A sickly drink, swallowed at first in tiny sips.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessively sugary, so cloying and sickly to taste.

clue.text: Communist pursuing former legal right? He believes in redistribution of wealth

definitions.text: He believes in redistribution of wealth

indicators.note: pursuing means the communist comes after the legal right

parts.note: soc was an old feudal right of jurisdiction
red is a common term for a communist

explanation.surface: A communist chases an ancient legal right, believing in sharing wealth.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter of Social Credit, a movement for distributing purchasing power to consumers.

clue.text: Team pack?

definitions.meaning: Wolverhampton Wanderers football club is known by this nickname
... run in packs, so the animals make up a pack

explanation.surface: A sports side and a pack of animals.
explanation.walkthrough: Wolves is the nickname of Wolverhampton Wanderers, an English football club.
explanation.definitionFit: A football side's nickname, and a set of predators that hunt in packs.

clue.text: Attractive youngsters to unite? About time

indicators.note: about means one piece goes round the other

parts.note: to tie is to bind together, unite

explanation.surface: Attractive young people look to marry in good time.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for attractive young women collectively, a set of eye candy.

clue.text: What Custer carried into battle leaders of Sioux at Bighorn easily ransacked

indicators.note: leaders of takes the first letter of each word that follows

explanation.surface: Custer's sword at the Little Bighorn, where the Sioux easily overran his camp.
explanation.walkthrough: Custer was a US cavalry general killed by the Sioux at the Little Bighorn in 1876.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavalry sword, the American spelling of sabre, carried by a mounted officer.

clue.text: Even though old-fashioned he wrote memorable plays

definitions.meaning: an archaic form meaning albeit, although
Edward ... wrote Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf?

explanation.surface: Though old-fashioned, he wrote plays to remember.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic conjunction meaning although, and the surname of an American dramatist.

clue.text: Sounds 'ostile in the front, having 18?

indicators.note: in says the noises are placed inside the word for the front

parts.note: fore means the front part
hostile sounds are hoots, and the dropped H in 'ostile asks us to drop it too

explanation.surface: Cockney jeers come from the front of the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sounds 'ostile' is Cockney 'oots, hoots without H. The definition reads 'having sore, tender feet', pointing back to 18.
explanation.definitionFit: Having sore, aching feet from walking; 18 describes tender soles, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Alternative to the Vulgate a Catholic mostly recalled

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word is turned round
mostly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Latin can mean Roman Catholic, as in the Latin church

explanation.surface: A Catholic recalls the old Bible translation he mostly used.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims LATIN to LATI, and 'recalled' turns it to ITAL.
explanation.definitionFit: An early Latin translation of the Bible, predating Jerome's Vulgate.

clue.text: Curls tight round either half of hair dressed in a bunch

indicators.note: tight round says the shuffled letters wrap closely around the hair
dressed suggests arranged anew, so the letters of curls are rearranged

parts.note: tete is a dressed head of hair, and either half of it gives the same pair of letters

explanation.surface: Tight curls round the head, styled in a bunch.
explanation.walkthrough: A tete is an old word for a dressed head of hair or hairpiece; 'dressed' rearranges the curls as CLUSR, which 'tight round' wraps about the pair.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of things gathered closely together, as grapes on a stem.

clue.text: Climbing lowest end of range, e.g. Atlas?

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the letters read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: net (nett) is the bottom-line figure, lowest after deductions

indicators.note: end of takes the last letter of range

explanation.surface: Climbing the lowest end of a mountain range such as the Atlas.
explanation.walkthrough: The Atlas Mountains are a range, but Atlas here is the Titan who held up the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for a giant, and the Titan Atlas was one.

clue.text: One should know how to negotiate traffic island, having ingested books

definitions.text: One should know how to negotiate traffic

indicators.note: having ingested says the island swallows the books

parts.note: a cay is a small low island
B is an abbreviation for book, so books are BB

explanation.surface: A traffic expert on a desert island, having swallowed a pile of books.
explanation.definitionFit: A taxi driver must know the roads and get through traffic.

clue.text: One taking time out, drained, in party? Same here

indicators.note: in places the pieces within the party

parts.note: a do is a party
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: drained means emptied, so only the outer letters of the phrase remain

explanation.surface: A partygoer takes a breather, drained, and says the same goes for him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drained' empties the phrase 'time out' to its outer letters, T and T.
explanation.definitionFit: Used to say the same applies, as in 'me too'.

clue.text: Take charge of restricting poverty, heavily involved

indicators.note: restricting means one piece holds the other within it

parts.note: to keep is to look after, take charge of
need means poverty, want

explanation.surface: Taking charge while hemmed in by poverty leaves one deeply involved.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for being deeply immersed in something, as if wading up to the knees.

clue.text: Deter getting led astray, in a corner

indicators.note: led astray means taken off course, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A deterrent led astray ends up cornered.
explanation.definitionFit: Chased up a tree by a pursuer, hence trapped and cornered.

clue.text: When traced back hereditary element reveals network

indicators.note: traced back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: as can mean when
a gene is a hereditary unit

explanation.surface: Tracing your ancestry reveals a network of genes.
explanation.definitionFit: A fishing net, a seine, so a mesh or network.
